title: Numeric types
description:
Write these functions in `solution.rs`:

```rust
fn to_celsius(fahrenheit: f64) -> f64                 // (F - 32) * 5 / 9
fn average(a: i32, b: i32, c: i32) -> f64            // exact: average(1, 2, 2) is 1.666...
fn to_cents(euros: f64) -> i64                        // rounded to the nearest cent: 19.99 gives 1999
fn add_volume(volume: u8, change: i16) -> u8         // stays within 0..=100 whatever the change
fn checked_area(width: u32, height: u32) -> Option<u32>   // None if the product overflows u32
```
hints: `(a + b + c)` with three large `i32`s overflows; convert each to `f64` first with `as f64`.

Convert the volume to a wider signed type (`volume as i16`) before adding a negative change, then `.clamp(0, 100)` and convert back: `x.clamp(lo, hi)` gives `lo` when `x` is smaller, `hi` when it is larger, and `x` otherwise.

`19.99 * 100.0` is not exactly 1999.0 in floating point, and `as i64` truncates toward zero; `x.round()` rounds an `f64` to the nearest whole number first. `checked_mul` works like `checked_add` from the lesson: `Some(product)`, or `None` on overflow.
